slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Boreal should decline exclusivity at signing and offer a nonexclusive pilot through which the OEM can earn limited exclusivity
The $2.0M is prepaid royalty, not new revenue; net of OEM costs, exclusivity earns $3.2M over three years at plan, $1.0M at 65%
–	Booking the advance on top of royalties overstates the deal by 23%
–	At 2027 plan volume, $40 of each $300 royalty is left after OEM costs
Exclusivity bars new direct licensing; at 65% of volumes it loses money in 2028 once over 36% of direct profit is lost
–	$1.48M of 2028 direct gross profit is at stake, with no data on how much goes
–	The growth case rests on five correlational cases and an unbooked forecast
Exclusivity at signing breaks the board's own conditions, and the work is fundable without the advance
–	Lab downtime ran at 2.4 times the OEM's limit, and the draft lacks six protections
–	Without the advance, a year of OEM costs leaves $0.55M above the buffer
Sign the nonexclusive pilot; grant limited exclusivity only after certification and audited volume
–	Pilot terms match exclusivity in 2028 even with a third fewer robots
–	Shipments, direct loss, support cost or audit rights could change it
